g.title: dependencies
g.text: Discrepancy and local statistics of modular inverses

a.xlink:title: Arithmetic shell norms enter the convex smoothing bound.
Arithmetic shells enter the separate general-boundary calculation.
Shell and rectangular moments control squared coefficients in the difference measure.
Squared shell and rectangular moments enter the variance estimates.
Convex brackets supply the geometric shell norms and integral error.
General brackets and translation control give boundary-dependent Fourier estimates.
Convex brackets and the one-dimensional adaptation give pointwise enclosure.
Convex Fourier tails and pointwise coefficients are applied without smoothing.
The counting identity evaluates the smooth brackets.
The counting identity is used in the general bracket reduction.
The difference Fourier identity supplies the nonnegative squared coefficients.
The indicator variance identity expresses the translation variance.
Dyadic sums control the shell contributions in the convex smoothing bound.
Use the dyadic lemma and its explicit constants; derive the near-zero exponent estimate separately.
The dyadic-summation lemma controls the smoothing sums.
Optimize the smoothing scale; then take a supremum or divide by the scaled area.
Shrinking-set equidistribution gives a uniform cutoff for distance.
Coordinate separation supplies the sufficient conditions for the exact one-point identity.
The disc variance yields an empty-disc tail estimate.
The elementary count and empty rectangle supply the two moment lower bounds.
